items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: you know the Bobby Scott tune?

ctx.x: Well as we go along we have more and more in common. I want to take you back, you mentioned Mr. DeAngelo, and can you recall the feeling or your reaction to the first time you heard one of your early arrangements played?
Oh yeah. I wrote my first big band chart for Sam when I was in high school. We had a quote stage band. And he was a piano player and an arranger and he wrote charts for the © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

band on things like “Comin’ Home Baby” and “So What.” I mean this was late 60s, early 70s. And I mean for the time, that was very hip for any kind of school band, college or high school. I mean this was a high school band. So the fact that he was writing charts for us was, this was so cool. So I got interested in writing and he encouraged me to write and I wrote this chart on “A Taste of Honey,” you know the Bobby Scott tune? So that was my first chart for a big band.
